title: Ledras Lament Scenes - Enhanced v7
author: Ledras Lament Team
global_structure: Ancient stone amphitheater viewed straight on. Six broad horizontal stone seating tiers rise from foreground to background. A seventh rear wall spans behind the upper tier. A tall rigid rectangular stone frame stands at the exact top-center position. The frame has straight vertical sides, a straight top edge, sharp corners and a clear rectangular opening. The amphitheater geometry, tier boundaries, frame proportions, frontal perspective and overall composition remain fixed and unchanged.
global_frame_rule: The central rectangular stone frame is a permanent architectural invariant. Do not move, distort, widen, narrow, tilt, decorate, replace or break it. Preserve its exact rectangular silhouette and vertical symmetry. Any moon or celestial disk must appear only inside the rectangular opening of the frame, never above, behind, beside or outside it.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.description: Night over the ancient amphitheater. A full moon appears centered inside the rectangular opening of the central stone frame. Star-filled sky, weathered limestone, soft desert sand, low drifting smoke and thin fog. Sparse traces of an ancient ruined landscape. Dark, mysterious and monumental atmosphere.
elements: circular moon light inside frame opening

subscenes.name: Intro - intro-start
subscenes.description: First stars appear over the silent amphitheater. The moon begins to rise inside the rectangular opening of the central stone frame, casting pale silver light across the weathered limestone tiers. Thin wisps of smoke drift upward from the lowest stage.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The rising moon through the frame opening mirrors the Phoenician lunar calendar's first day. In Cypro-Phoenician ritual sites, the rectangular stone opening (fenestella) frames celestial events as divine communication.

subscenes.name: Intro - intro-end
subscenes.description: The moon rises to center the frame opening. Stars fill the sky above. Low fog settles between the stone seating tiers. Ancient ruined landscape remnants catch the soft moonlight. The atmosphere deepens into quiet mystery.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The moon at frame-center marks the moment of celestial alignment. Cypriot megalithic structures commonly feature framed openings oriented to capture lunar standstills.

subscenes.name: Intro - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: The moon holds steady at the center of the stone frame. Starlight and moonlight balance across the amphitheater geometry. Drifting smoke moves in slow horizontal layers between tiers. The night breathes in a suspended moment.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The balanced moonlight across all six tiers reflects the Bronze Age principle of sacred geometry — the horizontal tiers representing the six directions of the earthly realm.

subscenes.name: Intro - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Deep night settles over the amphitheater. The moon at the center of the frame casts long silver shadows across the six stone tiers. Fog and smoke interweave around the stage. The ancient space feels watchful and still.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Deep night in Cypro-Phoenician tradition is the hour when the veil between the living world and the underworld grows thin. Smoke and fog carry prayers to the ancestors.

subscenes.name: Intro - end-begins
subscenes.description: The moon begins a subtle descent within the frame opening. Smoke thins and spreads into a high veil. Stars dim slightly as the deepest hour approaches. The atmosphere prepares for transition.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The moon's descent signals the closing of the nightly ritual window. In ancient Cypriot practice, the hour before dawn belongs to the chthonic deities.

subscenes.name: Intro - end-final
subscenes.description: Minimal moonlight remains. Smoke dissipates to almost nothing. The amphitheater exists in near-silhouette, its geometry suggested by starlight alone. A held breath before dawn.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Starlit silence before dawn echoes the Phoenician concept of 'raqia' — the moment of cosmic pause between cycles, when creation holds its breath before renewal.

scenes.name: Ritual
scenes.description: Nighttime ritual within the fixed ancient amphitheater. A full moon appears centered inside the rectangular opening of the central stone frame. Spiritual ethno-Cypriot letterforms appear as luminous symbolic shapes inside the frame, then conceptually descend toward the center of the lowest stage area. Dark red sparks and subtle glowing particles circle around a still lying human form at the bottom-center stage. Mystical, solemn and restrained atmosphere.

subscenes.name: Ritual - intro-start
subscenes.description: The moon glows at the center of the stone frame. Faint luminous shapes begin to form within the frame opening — ethno-Cypriot symbolic glyphs flickering like distant lamps. The still human form lies at the bottom-center stage. The ritual has not yet begun.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The first appearance of luminous letterforms evokes the Cypro-Phoenician syllabary, a script native to Cyprus from the 11th–4th centuries BCE. These glyphs were used exclusively for ritual and funerary inscriptions.

subscenes.name: Ritual - intro-end
subscenes.description: The luminous letterforms intensify and begin a slow descent from the frame toward the stage. Dark red sparks appear and orbit the central space. The still figure at the bottom-center is haloed by faint particles. The ritual awakens.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The descending letterforms symbolize the Eteocypriot belief in written prayer as a physical bridge between worshiper and deity — words that travel downward into the earth.

subscenes.name: Ritual - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Symbolic glyphs hover in the air between the frame and the stage, glowing with restrained spiritual light. Dark red sparks circle the supine figure in a steady procession. Particles drift through the six tiers. The ritual finds its rhythm.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The orbiting sparks mirror archaeological evidence of ritual fire-handling in Cypriot sanctuaries. Priests would circle the altar with lamps and censing vessels.

subscenes.name: Ritual - loop-middle
subscenes.description: The luminous letterforms pulse gently in a repeating cycle. Sparks continue their orbit around the bottom-center figure. Smoke and particle trails weave through the amphitheater. The ritual sustains its solemn intensity.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The supine figure represents the ritual practitioner in trance. Eteocypriot temple sites contain stone platforms interpreted as incubation beds for oracular dreaming.

subscenes.name: Ritual - end-begins
subscenes.description: The glyphs begin to fade, their light withdrawing upward toward the frame. Sparks diminish to occasional embers. The still figure rests in growing shadow. The ritual exhales.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The fading glyphs suggest the oracle withdrawing. In Cypro-Phoenician practice, the moment of silence after ritual speech was as sacred as the words themselves.

subscenes.name: Ritual - end-final
subscenes.description: The last traces of luminous forms dissolve within the frame opening. A few embers glow on the stone floor. The human form remains motionless in near-darkness. The amphitheater returns to its ancient silence.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Final stillness echoes the Phoenician 'shalem' — the state of completeness after ritual, when the divine presence returns to its realm leaving the material world untouched.

scenes.name: Astarte Awakens
scenes.description: The night amphitheater remains structurally unchanged. The moon centered inside the rectangular opening of the central stone frame transforms from bright white into a deep red blood moon. Desert sand and warm yellow limestone dominate the surrounding environment. The atmosphere becomes intense, sacred and foreboding.

subscenes.name: Astarte Awakens - intro-start
subscenes.description: The moon within the frame opening begins to shift — a faint reddish tint spreads from its center outward. The limestone walls catch a warm glow. The atmosphere subtly changes, gaining weight and anticipation.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The blood moon transformation invokes the Canaanite goddess Astarte's descent narrative. In Ugaritic texts, the moon darkens as she passes through the underworld gates. Transformation begins at the lunar limen.

subscenes.name: Astarte Awakens - intro-end
subscenes.description: The blood moon deepens to a rich red, fully transformed at the center of the frame. Warm shadows fall across the six tiers. Yellow limestone reflects the crimson light. Sacred tension builds across the amphitheater.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Deep red illumination over the limestone recalls the ritual blood sacrifices of the Phoenician tophet. The limestone absorbs warmth as the sacred precinct receives the offering.

subscenes.name: Astarte Awakens - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: The blood moon burns at full intensity within the rectangular frame opening. The entire amphitheater is bathed in deep red light. Limestone glows warm amber. The space holds its breath in sacred foreboding.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The fully crimson moon at frame-center mirrors the 'hrn' (sacred enclosure) of Cypriot open-air sanctuaries, where a framed view of the sky focused sacrificial attention.

subscenes.name: Astarte Awakens - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Intense crimson light radiates steadily from the blood moon. The tier surfaces show stark red-and-amber contrasts. The atmosphere remains at peak sacred tension, suspended in time.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Sustained sacred intensity reflects the Phoenician concept of 'qadosh' — a state of maintained holiness that requires continuous ritual attention to prevent dissipation.

subscenes.name: Astarte Awakens - end-begins
subscenes.description: The blood moon begins to cool, red receding toward a muted rose. Shadows soften. The limestone warm glow starts to fade. Sacred intensity slowly releases its hold.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The receding red symbolizes Astarte's return journey. In the mythology, the goddess must re-emerge with gifts of dawn, leaving traces of divine fire on the stones she passes.

subscenes.name: Astarte Awakens - end-final
subscenes.description: The moon returns to a pale white, blood transformation complete. Normal moonlight restores silver tones across the amphitheater. Traces of warmth linger on the stone. The sacred moment has passed.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The return to pale moonlight represents cosmic equilibrium restored. Cypro-Phoenician theology prized balance — the goddess's transformation is a cycle, not a permanent alteration.

scenes.name: Water Emergence
scenes.description: The ancient amphitheater remains structurally fixed while the surrounding desert gradually transforms into a living landscape. Desert sand gives way to greenery, low plants and flourishing trees growing naturally around and between the stone tiers. Subtle narrow water channels appear within existing stone surfaces without changing the tier geometry. Quiet nighttime atmosphere with soft natural illumination.

subscenes.name: Water Emergence - intro-start
subscenes.description: Barely visible moisture glistens on the lowest stone tier surfaces. A subtle dampness spreads across the desert sand at the amphitheater base. The first hint of transformation — water touching ancient stone.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The first moisture on stone mirrors the Cypriot karst spring phenomenon — water emerging from limestone after seasonal rains. In ancient Cyprus, these sudden springs were considered divine gifts.

subscenes.name: Water Emergence - intro-end
subscenes.description: Narrow water channels emerge along the existing tier boundaries. Thin streams trace the horizontal geometry without altering it. Moisture darkens the stone. Green shoots appear at the edges of the water paths.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Water channels following the tier boundaries reflect the Bronze Age qanat irrigation systems used across Cyprus. These underground channels brought water without altering surface geography.

subscenes.name: Water Emergence - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Water flows steadily through the established channels, following the tier geometry. Shallow pools form on lower surfaces. Low greenery and small plants grow around the water lines. The transformation gains momentum.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The flowing water symbolizes the Phoenician deity Melqart, associated with springs and renewal. His sanctuaries were always built near natural watercourses.

subscenes.name: Water Emergence - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Flourishing greenery frames the water channels. Narrow streams cascade gently between tiers. Trees and shrubs grow naturally around the stone architecture. The amphitheater hosts a living landscape without losing its form.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The integration of wet and dry elements mirrors the Cypro-Phoenician concept of 'harmonia' — a balance of opposites maintained by sacred architecture.

subscenes.name: Water Emergence - end-begins
subscenes.description: Water flow begins to slow. Greenery reaches full growth but activity quiets. The streams narrow slightly. The living landscape settles into equilibrium with the ancient stone.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Slowing water suggests the end of the wet season. In Cypriot agricultural ritual, the closing of irrigation channels was marked with a simple offering to the spring spirit.

subscenes.name: Water Emergence - end-final
subscenes.description: Still water pools reflect starlight. Greenery rustles in a faint breeze. The water channels lie calm, their work complete. The amphitheater rests in its transformed state.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Still pools reflecting starlight recall the sacred springs of Kourion, where ritual mirrors were used to capture moonlight for divination into the Roman period.

scenes.name: Balance
scenes.description: Water enters the fixed ancient amphitheater in harmony with the existing architecture. Calm streams and narrow canals follow the natural horizontal and vertical stone geometry without altering the six tiers. Water gently cascades between existing levels and creates reflective surfaces. Trees, crops and spring vegetation grow around the edges and between stone structures. Leaves and crops suggest a gentle wind. Nighttime atmosphere with subtle reflections, abundance and balance between stone, water and life.

subscenes.name: Balance - intro-start
subscenes.description: Early morning light casts golden reflections across the water surfaces in the fixed amphitheater. The calm streams and narrow canals catch the first rays of sunlight, creating rippled patterns of light and shadow. Vegetation sways gently in the soft morning breeze. The balance between architectural permanence and natural abundance is perfectly captured in this tranquil dawn moment.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Golden hour lighting emphasizes the harmony between natural and architectural elements

subscenes.name: Balance - intro-end
subscenes.description: Morning light warms the stone as the canals carry steady water through the amphitheater. Sunlight catches the rippling surfaces, casting shifting patterns across the tier faces. Vegetation along the water edges sways gently.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Following the dawn, morning light in Cyprus was the hour for ritual water blessing. Priests would trace the canal paths with olive branches, sanctifying the flow for the day ahead.

subscenes.name: Balance - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Midday light reaches through the frame opening, illuminating the central canal system. Water cascades between tiers in a steady rhythm. Leaves and crops move in a light breeze. The balance between architecture and nature is fully realized.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Midday light at its zenith represents the moment of spiritual fullness. In Cypro-Phoenician temples, noon was the hour of the goring — for sacrifice.

subscenes.name: Balance - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Afternoon shadows lengthen across the water surfaces. Reflections shift from bright gold to deeper amber. The canals continue their calm flow. Vegetation rustles in the warm air. A sustained moment of natural harmony.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Afternoon shadows lengthening recall the Phoenician practice of 'tzaharayim' — the splitting light, when sunlight angles shift from one direction to another, marking the transition.

subscenes.name: Balance - end-begins
subscenes.description: As day turns to night, warm sunset light reflects off the water surfaces creating intimate pools of golden light. The gentle breeze continues to move through the vegetation, suggesting life continues even as activity slows. The balance maintained by the water architecture creates a peaceful transition between day and night in this contemplative twilight scene.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Twilight lighting creates romantic intimacy while preserving structural permanence

subscenes.name: Balance - end-final
subscenes.description: Night settles over the water-filled amphitheater. The moon appears inside the frame opening, reflected in the calm canals below. Water surfaces mirror starlight. The architecture and the living landscape rest together in silence.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Night water reflections mirror the Cypriot tradition of 'hydrophany' — pools used as divination mirrors. Still water reflecting the moon was read for omens by temple attendants.

scenes.name: Overflow
scenes.description: Water persists throughout the fixed ancient amphitheater. Vegetation becomes increasingly abundant as if observed through a slow natural time-lapse. Trees, grasses, vines and greenery gradually fill spaces around the existing stone tiers while the architecture remains completely still and unchanged. Water continues calmly through the established channels. Quiet, fertile, abundant and dreamlike atmosphere.

subscenes.name: Overflow - intro-start
subscenes.description: Water continues its patient flow through the amphitheater channels. Vines begin to climb the lower stone tiers. Greenery thickens along the water paths, extending upward between the ancient seats.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The vines climbing the stone tiers echo archaeological evidence of grape cultivation on Cyprus terraces since the Early Bronze Age. The vine was sacred to Aphrodite Cyprus.

subscenes.name: Overflow - intro-end
subscenes.description: Vegetation spreads visibly across the six tiers. Grasses fill the gaps between stones. Vines reach higher up the tier faces. The architecture remains unchanged, cradling the growing abundance.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Grass filling stone gaps reflects the Phoenician reverence for spontaneous growth in sacred precincts. Unmanaged vegetation was considered evidence of divine presence.

subscenes.name: Overflow - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Abundant greenery surrounds every level of the amphitheater. Trees overhang the upper tiers. Vines frame the central stone opening. Water moves calmly through the lush channels. The space feels alive and fertile.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The framing of the stone opening by greenery recalls the sacred groves (alsos) of Cypriot sanctuaries, where nature and architecture formed a unified ritual space.

subscenes.name: Overflow - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Maximum abundance — greenery pours over tiers and around the stone frame. Leaves, blossoms, and climbing plants create a rich living tapestry. Water continues its quiet flow beneath the vegetation. Dreamlike fertility.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Maximum abundance mirrors the Cypro-Phoenician harvest festival of 'Elul', when the temple precinct was allowed to reach its most fertile state before the first reaping.

subscenes.name: Overflow - end-begins
subscenes.description: Growth slows, reaching a plateau. The vegetation is fully established, moving gently in the night air. Water channels remain active. The abundance feels not chaotic but deliberate, as if the stone chose to host the green.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The plateau of growth represents the state of 'satedness' in Phoenician agricultural theology — enough abundance granted by the gods, beyond which desire becomes greed.

subscenes.name: Overflow - end-final
subscenes.description: The lush amphitheater rests in moonlight. Leaves and vines gleam with dew. Water surfaces are still, reflecting stars and the moon inside the frame. The living and the ancient coexist in tranquil permanence.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Dew-covered vegetation at rest recalls the 'tal' (dew) of Phoenician blessing texts — considered the gentlest form of divine favor, sufficient without overwhelming.

scenes.name: Wind
scenes.description: The fixed ancient amphitheater becomes dominated by wind and drifting smoke. Thin layers of smoke move horizontally and diagonally across the existing stone tiers without obscuring their geometry. Smoke gathers around the bottom-center stage and rises gently through the rectangular opening of the central stone frame. The atmosphere is ethereal, weightless and mysterious.

subscenes.name: Wind - intro-start
subscenes.description: Thin wisps of white smoke begin to rise from the lowest stage, curling upward through the tier levels. The air grows hazy. A gentle wind stirs the smoke into elongated strands that drift horizontally.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The first smoke rising from the stage echoes the Cypro-Phoenician practice of incense offerings (labonah) from ground-level altars. White smoke was believed to carry prayers upward through the stone tiers.

subscenes.name: Wind - intro-end
subscenes.description: Smoke layers build across the amphitheater — horizontal bands moving between the six stone tiers. Wind carries smoke diagonally across the stage. The frame opening begins to catch and channel the drifting haze.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Smoke layering between tiers mirrors the stratified cosmology of Eteocypriot religion — six horizontal planes between earth and sky, each with its own spirit realm.

subscenes.name: Wind - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Smoke moves in steady streams across the amphitheater geometry, following the tier lines. A column of smoke rises gently through the rectangular frame opening. The wind shapes it into ethereal spirals.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The smoke column passing through the frame opening reflects the sacred 'axis mundi' concept. In Phoenician temples, a central opening in the roof channeled sacrificial smoke to the heavens.

subscenes.name: Wind - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Maximum smoke movement — horizontal layers sweep across every tier. A continuous stream passes through the frame opening and disperses above. The amphitheater appears to breathe smoke, weightless and alive.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Maximum movement of smoke through all six tiers symbolizes the complete communication between the earthly and divine realms — every spiritual layer activated simultaneously.

subscenes.name: Wind - end-begins
subscenes.description: Wind calms. Smoke layers thin and separate. The frame opening releases the last steady column upward. Remaining haze settles in the lower tiers. The ethereal intensity dissipates.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Wind calming and smoke thinning represent the closing of the divine channel. In Cypriot ritual, the wind had to be explicitly dismissed at ceremony's end.

subscenes.name: Wind - end-final
subscenes.description: Only faint traces of smoke remain, hovering at ground level. The wind has stilled completely. The amphitheater geometry is fully visible again through the clear night air. A quiet after the breath.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The stillness after the wind recalls the Phoenician term 'd'mamah' — a thin silence, the state of the sacred space between visitations, always waiting.

scenes.name: Village
scenes.description: A calm nighttime village emerges within the existing amphitheater without changing the stone tier geometry. Warm miniature home lights appear integrated into the tier surfaces and existing architectural spaces. Small village-like illuminated details are distributed across the layered amphitheater while the six horizontal tiers remain clearly visible and structurally unchanged. Fireflies drift through the air. Existing greenery moves gently in the wind. Warm human presence is suggested through light, but no modern city architecture.

subscenes.name: Village - intro-start
subscenes.description: The first warm lights appear within the stone tiers — small glowing windows embedded in the ancient architecture. Village life begins to emerge. A few fireflies drift across the lower stage.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Warm lights embedded in stone tiers follow the Bronze Age pattern of rock-cut dwellings at Kition and Hala Sultan Tekke, where homes were carved directly into existing stone formations.

subscenes.name: Village - intro-end
subscenes.description: More windows illuminate across the six tiers. The village takes shape within the stone geometry — warm orange light pools against weathered limestone. Fireflies increase, floating through the evening air.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Spreading evening lights mimic the Cypriot custom of lighting household lamps at sunset — 'lychnapsia' — the ritual lighting of oil lamps throughout the village.

subscenes.name: Village - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Celebration night in the amphitheater village. Lanterns and decorative lights enhance the warm miniature architecture. Villagers gather in the spaces between stone tiers, creating a lively atmosphere while maintaining the ancient geometric constraints. The lighting creates a festive yet authentic scene that respects the architectural permanence.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Festival lighting adds cultural vibrancy while maintaining architectural integrity

subscenes.name: Village - loop-middle
subscenes.description: The village hums with quiet activity. Lights glow steadily from homes embedded in the tier architecture. Fireflies drift in lazy patterns between the stone levels. Warm smoke rises from cooking fires. A living community within ancient walls.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Quiet community activity mirrors the daily market and gathering rhythms of ancient Cypriot village life. The agora was the heart of the settlement where daily exchange occurred.

subscenes.name: Village - end-begins
subscenes.description: Autumn harvest celebration within the amphitheater. Warm light from home fires reflects on surfaces, suggesting abundance and community. Villagers gather crops and provisions, their activities following the natural patterns established by the stone geometry. The harvest scene emphasizes community and seasonal cycles within the ancient space.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Harvest activities emphasize community and seasonal rhythms within architectural constraints

subscenes.name: Village - end-final
subscenes.description: The village quiets as night deepens. Most windows dim to embers. A few fireflies remain, their glow fading. The stone tiers return to near-darkness with only occasional warm pinpoints of light. The village sleeps within the ancient amphitheater.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The village falling asleep mirrors the ancient Cypriot concept of 'eudaimonia' — the well-lived life, where community activity yields to rest in a cycle renewed each dawn.

scenes.name: Fire
scenes.description: The fixed ancient amphitheater burns during the night. Fire follows the existing horizontal tier boundaries without changing their geometry. Remaining greenery burns and glows. A deep red blood moon appears centered only inside the rectangular opening of the central stone frame. Flames surround the frame while preserving its rigid rectangular silhouette. A thin elegant blood-red canal flows downward through the existing architecture toward the bottom-center stage. Tragic, monumental and ritualistic atmosphere.

subscenes.name: Fire - intro-start
subscenes.description: Small flames wake along the lowest tier edges, licking at the ancient stone. The blood moon begins to redden inside the frame. Thin trails of smoke rise from the first burning greenery.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The first flames waking on stone echo the Cypro-Phoenician foundation rite — fire was used to 'wake' new stone constructions. The heat was believed to summon the earth spirit into the architecture.

subscenes.name: Fire - intro-end
subscenes.description: Fire spreads along the horizontal tier boundaries, following the stone geometry precisely. The blood moon reaches full crimson at the center of the frame. A thin line of glowing red begins to flow down from the stage — the first trace of the blood canal.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Fire spreading along tier boundaries reflects the controlled burn practices of ancient Cypriot agriculture, where fire was guided along stone field boundaries without damaging the structure.

subscenes.name: Fire - loop-start-end
subscenes.description: Flames dance across all six tiers, contained within the architectural lines. The blood moon burns at the center of the frame, surrounded by fire. The blood-red canal flows steadily from the stage downward through the lower tiers.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The blood-red canal invokes the Phoenician funerary practice of pouring red ochre water through tombs — a symbolic blood offering intended to feed the spirits of the ancestors.

subscenes.name: Fire - loop-middle
subscenes.description: Peak fire — every tier edge lined with flame. The blood moon glows at maximum intensity within the frame opening. The red canal runs bright and continuous. The amphitheater burns in ritualistic majesty without losing its structure.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Peak conflagration mirrors the Cypriot tradition of the 'purification pyre' — a ritual burning within a confined sacred space that cleanses without destroying the containing architecture.

subscenes.name: Fire - end-begins
subscenes.description: Flames lower, their height decreasing. The blood canal narrows. The moon remains red but less intense. Embers glow across the stone surfaces. The tragic fire approaches its conclusion.
subscenes.cultural_notes: Lowering flames symbolize the withdrawal of divine fire. In Cypro-Phoenician ritual, the fire god Kothar would only remain present as long as the flames rose.

subscenes.name: Fire - end-final
subscenes.description: Fire reduces to glowing embers along the tier edges. The blood canal thins to a dark trickle. The moon returns toward white. Smoke rises from the cooled stone. The amphitheater stands scarred but intact, its geometry preserved.
subscenes.cultural_notes: The amphitheater scarred but intact represents the central Phoenician theological principle of permanence through transformation — form endures while substance changes.

style_seed: Cypro-Phoenician and Levantine Bronze Age ruin style. Weathered limestone, ashlar sandstone, mudbrick traces and ancient stone construction. Restrained ornamentation. No Doric or Ionic columns, no Classical Greek temple architecture, no Parthenon silhouettes, no white marble monuments.
